actions.detail: Preflight and WorkPreflight froze roles -> policies -> grants -> two-tenant tests -> diff under local Phase 3 dependency projections.

The isolated migration role is non-superuser, has no CREATEROLE, and has no BYPASSRLS. Test-only principals therefore require explicit fixture provisioning by the isolated cluster owner before migration.
Added five pre-provisioned NOBYPASSRLS role fixtures, least-privilege grants, FORCE RLS on ten Runtime tables, direct and inherited tenant policies, and a forward-fix-only rollback boundary.

The first fixture setup assumed a conventional postgres administrator role, but the isolated cluster has no such role. A read-only pg_roles query identified gonow_bootstrap_admin as the task-owned superuser/CREATEROLE identity; the fixture now binds that exact local role. No migration or RLS assertion had executed before failure.

The next run exposed a distinct fixture defect: two tenants were seeded in one transaction, so tenant A's deferred receipt guard observed the intentionally switched tenant B context at commit and failed closed. Seeding now uses one fixed server-derived tenant per transaction; no policy or trigger was relaxed.

Five real PostgreSQL RLS tests passed after fixture repair, covering CT-007, three roles across two tenants, missing context, cross-tenant writes, role separation, exact policy/grant catalog, and forward-fix rollback.
Added exact P03-007 Verify, Security, Evidence, WorksetVerify, and RollbackVerify adapters without changing Catalog bytes.
The complete Agent CI suite passed after the RLS repair: 200 unit/integration tests and 42 contract tests, plus formatting, lint, type, secret, license, dependency-audit, and clock-contract checks.
